name: Big Angus
description: A prize fighter whom no one has ever beaten in bare-knuckle fighting; in a story seed, grogs can win back lost money by defeating him.

name: Advanced Group Combat
description: Optional rules expanding ArM5 group combat with more tactical depth, including accelerated training and leader actions.

name: Group Combat
description: ArM5 rules letting characters fight as a group with a leader and vanguard, sharing a combat bonus and inflicting Damage per member.

name: Trained Group
description: A group that has practiced fighting together for a season (or less with accelerated training) and functions with the trained group rules.

name: Accelerated Group Training
description: Rule letting a leader shorten a group's training time with a Communication + Leadership + stress die roll against an Ease Factor based on time available.

name: Group Leader
description: The character commanding a group in combat; issuing orders is usually a fast action and the leader's Presence + Leadership governs Discipline, Morale and rallying.

name: Vanguard
description: The member of a group whose statistics drive its attacks; a group with no vanguard can't attack and the leader may designate a new one as a fast action.

name: Fast Action
description: An optional combat action type; issuing orders, designating a vanguard, or shooting a loaded crossbow with Ready Missiles can be fast actions.

name: Morale and Discipline
description: Optional rules that weaken groups while making the leader more important, requiring Discipline and Morale rolls in battle.

name: Discipline Roll
description: A reaction roll (leader's Presence + Leadership + stress die) required when a group is tempted to break formation; failure makes the group disordered.

name: Morale Roll
description: A reaction roll (leader's Presence + Leadership + stress die) made when bad things happen on the battlefield; failure disorders or routs the group.

name: Disordered Group
description: A group that failed a Discipline or Morale check; trained groups function as untrained, and untrained disordered groups hit only half as often.

name: Routed Group
description: A group that has lost its will to fight and tries to disengage and flee; results from a disordered group failing a Morale check.

name: Rallying a Group
description: A leader's action (Presence + Leadership + stress die) that improves a routed group to disordered or restores a disordered group to normal.

name: Casualty
description: A group member with a Medium Wound or worse, unconscious, or unable to fight due to magic; casualties raise the Ease Factor to rally.

name: Personality Trait
description: Character traits such as Loyal and Brave; positive scores across a group grant bonuses to Discipline and Morale rolls.

name: Loyal
description: Personality Trait; if all group members have a positive Loyal score, the group adds the lowest score to Discipline rolls.

name: Brave
description: Personality Trait; if all group members have a positive Brave score, the group adds the lowest score to Morale rolls.

name: Inspirational
description: A Virtue that may provide a bonus to shortening group training time if the storyguide sees fit.

name: Difficult Underlings
description: A Flaw that most likely imposes a penalty on shortening group training time.

name: Leadership
description: Ability used in commanding groups: shortening training, Discipline, Morale, rallying, replacing a vanguard, and assuming leadership.

name: Communication
description: Characteristic combined with Leadership to shorten group training time.

name: Presence
description: Characteristic combined with Leadership for Discipline, Morale, rallying and assuming leadership rolls.

name: Brawl
description: Weapon Ability used for unarmed attacks, kicks, gauntlets, bludgeons, daggers and knives.

name: Single Weapon
description: Weapon Ability for one-handed weapons such as axes, maces, swords, spears and shields; also used with nets and whips to trip or disarm.

name: Great Weapon
description: Weapon Ability for two-handed weapons such as cudgels, flails, halberds, pole axes, great swords, staves and warhammers.

name: Thrown Weapon
description: Weapon Ability for thrown missiles such as throwing axes, javelins, knives, slings and stones.

name: Bows
description: Weapon Ability used for bows, composite bows, horse bows and longbows.

name: Crossbows
description: Weapon Ability used for crossbows and arbalests; untrained use does not add the usual extra botch dice.

name: Edge of the Razor
description: Spell (ArM5 p.154) that only works on edged or pointed weapons.

name: Longevity Ritual
description: Ritual allowing magi to live far longer, e.g. from a 1220 saga start into the 14th century.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The setting of Ars Magica, whose history need not parallel the real world.

name: Western Roman Empire
description: Empire whose collapse around 480 AD marks the end of the ancient period for equipment availability.

name: Imperial Rome
description: Roman empire that used the lorica segmentata and the scutum of the legionary.

name: Wales
description: Region to which longbows were historically confined for most of the high Middle Ages.

name: Saracens
description: People who use the composite bow.

name: Moors
description: People who use the composite bow.

name: Mongols
description: Asiatic nomads using the composite bow; the Mongol saber is a long sword variant.

name: Turks
description: Asiatic nomads who use the composite bow.

name: Huns
description: Early medieval Asiatic nomads who used the composite bow.

name: Magyars
description: Early medieval nomads who used the composite bow.

name: Faerie Knights
description: A court of faerie knights that whisks grogs from their covenant and subjects them to martial challenges in a story seed.

name: Faerie
description: Faeries appear with archaic equipment, primitive sharpened rocks, tree-bark armor and exotic armor.

name: Grog
description: Covenant soldiers/servants who fight in groups and are outfitted with armor.

name: Turb
description: The covenant's band of grogs, targeted by faerie sport in a story seed.

name: Equipment Availability
description: Classification of weapons and armor by historical period (ancient, early, high, late medieval) or region.

name: Quality of Arms and Armor
description: Rules from City & Guild for shoddy, standard, superior and excellent items; superior/excellent items grant bonuses, shoddy ones break easily.

name: Weapon Damage Types
description: Weapons are categorized as crushing, piercing or slashing by the injuries they cause, relevant to magical effects.

name: Blunted Weapon
description: Slashing or piercing weapons blunted for tournaments, subtracting 3 from Damage.

name: Stone Weapons
description: Primitive weapons that deal 2 less Damage than metal ones, minimum +1.

name: Try Using the Other End
description: Optional rule giving a -1 Attack penalty when a weapon deals its secondary damage type.

name: Clash of Weapons
description: Optional rule checking for weapon breakage when Attack Total exactly equals Defense Total.

name: Weapon Breakage
description: Stress die + Weapon Ability vs. Ease Factor 9 (15 for improvised weapons); failure loses a damage level.

name: Damage Levels
description: How many damage levels a weapon or shield sustains before breaking; most have two, spears and lances one.

name: Ready Missiles
description: Combat option under which shooting a loaded crossbow is a fast action.

name: Spanning
description: Extended Action needed to load a crossbow, its length depending on the mechanism (belt hook, windlass, cranequin, goat's foot).

name: Mounted Archery
description: Rules for shooting from horseback, relevant to the horse bow.

name: Falling from Horseback
description: Rule for damage taken when a rider falls or is unseated.

name: Unseat
description: Non-lethal special effect dragging a rider from the saddle; possible with halberds, pole arms, nets and whips.

name: Disarm
description: Non-lethal special effect making the opponent's weapon fall; retrieving it requires an action and disengaging.

name: Wrest Weapon
description: Non-lethal action leaving the attacker holding the opponent's weapon or other item like a wizard's staff.

name: Non-Lethal Combat
description: Optional combat rules with special effects like disarm, unseat and wrest weapon.

name: Penalty for Fighting Without a Helmet
description: Optional rule adding an extra botch die to melee Defense and Evasion rolls for characters without head protection.

name: Complex Armor Design
description: Optional rules to build armor from materials by body area and Load Factor, useful for faerie or historical armor.

name: Expanded Armor Rules
description: Rules expanding ArM5 armor with more materials and a component system of body armor, surcoat/greaves and helmet.

name: Load
description: Encumbrance value of weapons and armor.

name: Protection
description: Armor's defensive value, computed by summing body armor, surcoat and helmet.

name: Encumbrance
description: ArM5 rules (p.178) governing Load.

name: Gauntlet
description: Brawl weapon or hand armor.

name: Bludgeon
description: Inexpensive crushing Brawl weapon.

name: Dagger
description: Piercing/slashing Brawl weapon.

name: Knife
description: Brawl weapon that can also be thrown.

name: Axe
description: Single weapon dealing slashing damage.

name: Club
description: Inexpensive crushing single weapon.

name: Short Dueling Stick
description: Ancient single-weapon crushing stick.

name: Falchion
description: Heavy one-handed machete-like weapon used by common soldiers; late medieval.

name: Hatchet
description: Inexpensive slashing single weapon.

name: Lance
description: Piercing single weapon of the high period with only one damage level.

name: Mace
description: Crushing single weapon.

name: Mace and Chain
description: Early medieval crushing single weapon.

name: Net
description: Weapon usable to trip, grapple, disarm or unseat a rider; otherwise ineffective.

name: Spear
description: Piercing single weapon with one damage level.

name: Short Sword
description: One-handed piercing/slashing sword.

name: Long Sword
description: Expensive single weapon with variations such as the spatha and Mongol saber.

name: Spatha
description: Late Roman variation on the long sword.

name: Mongol Saber
description: Mongol variation on the long sword.

name: Buckler
description: Small shield of the high period.

name: Round Shield
description: Inexpensive shield.

name: Heater Shield
description: High-period shield granting +3 Defense.

name: Infantry Shield
description: Large shield usable only on foot, such as the Roman scutum.

name: Scutum
description: Convex rectangular shield of the Roman legionary.

name: Trident
description: Ancient piercing weapon.

name: Whip
description: Poor weapon usable to trip, grapple, disarm or unseat.

name: Cudgel
description: Inexpensive two-handed crushing weapon.

name: Farm Implement
description: Improvised two-handed weapon.

name: Flail
description: Two-handed crushing weapon.

name: Halberd
description: Late-medieval pole axe with a spike and hook for dragging riders from horses.

name: Pole Arm
description: Two-handed weapon usable to unseat a rider.

name: Pole Axe
description: Two-handed slashing weapon.

name: Long Spear
description: Two-handed piercing weapon including the boar spear.

name: Great Sword
description: Late medieval two-handed sword.

name: Staff
description: Two-handed crushing weapon.

name: Warhammer
description: Two-handed crushing weapon.

name: Bastard Sword
description: Late-medieval sword usable one- or two-handed.

name: Throwing Axe
description: Thrown slashing weapon.

name: Javelin
description: Thrown piercing weapon.

name: Sling
description: Thrown missile weapon.

name: Sharpened Rock
description: Very primitive thrown weapon sometimes used by faeries.

name: Bow
description: New name for the short bow.

name: Composite Bow
description: Bow used by Saracens, Moors and Asiatic nomads.

name: Horse Bow
description: Compact composite bow suited to horseback.

name: Longbow
description: Late bow historically confined to Wales, signature English weapon after 1283.

name: Crossbow
description: Missile weapon spanned with a belt hook; Strength does not add to Damage.

name: Arbalest
description: Crossbow requiring a mechanical device such as a windlass to span.

name: Heavy Arbalest
description: Late-medieval steel-bowed arbalest spanned by a cranequin.

name: Padded Armor
description: Inexpensive armor of quilted fabric, felt, or stuffed leather.

name: Boiled Leather
description: Tough stiff armor material; cuir boulli is a variant.

name: Reinforced Armor
description: Leather or padding strengthened with small plates or rings.

name: Rigid Scale
description: Non-metallic scale or lamellar armor.

name: Metal Scale
description: Metal lamellar armor, including brigandine.

name: Mail
description: Chain mail; mail shirts ancient, full mail early medieval.

name: Plate Armor
description: Armor of solid metal pieces; full Gothic plate is late medieval.

name: Plate and Mail
description: Mail strengthened with metal plates.

name: Gambeson
description: Garment of padded material worn over, under or instead of armor; also aketon or arming jacket.

name: Coat of Plates
description: Lamellar cuirass worn over mail c.1250-1300.

name: Greaves
description: Armor for the lower legs.

name: Jambes
description: Plate armor covering the legs.

name: Ailettes
description: Boiled leather shoulder plates.

name: Aketon
description: Padded jacket worn under a mail hauberk.

name: Bascinet
description: Late medieval fitted helmet with visor.

name: Brigandine
description: Late armor of small plates riveted to canvas or leather.

name: Camail
description: Mail hood covering head, forehead, lower face.

name: Iron Cap
description: Helmet protecting the crown of the head.

name: Chausses
description: Mail leggings.

name: Coif
description: Open-faced mail hood.

name: Cuirass
description: Breastplate and backplate.

name: Cuir Boulli
description: Boiled leather made by boiling in oil.

name: Fauld
description: Lamellar hip protection.

name: Gorget
description: Stiff collar protecting throat and neck.

name: Hauberk
description: Knee-length long-sleeved coat of flexible armor.

name: Haubergeon
description: Short-sleeved armored tunic.

name: Open Helmet
description: Helmet leaving the face half exposed.

name: Helm
description: High-medieval headgear encasing head and neck.

name: Jack
description: Brigandine jerkin, late medieval.

name: Jerkin
description: Short sleeveless jacket.

name: Kettle Hat
description: Bowl-shaped iron cap with wide brim.

name: Lamellar
description: Overlapping plates fastened to each other.

name: Lorica Hamata
description: Roman mail haubergeon.

name: Lorica Segmentata
description: Imperial Roman lamellar cuirass.

name: Poleyns
description: Knee protectors.

name: Ring Armor
description: Early medieval leather armor with rings.

name: Sabaton
description: Foot armor.

name: Sallet
description: Late medieval rounded helmet with visor.

name: Scale Armor
description: Small overlapping plates on backing.

name: Vambraces
description: Arm armor.

name: Cranequin
description: Mechanical device for spanning a heavy arbalest.

name: Goat's Foot
description: Late-medieval lever for spanning a crossbow.

name: Windlass
description: Device used to span arbalests.
